articleTitle: Vehicle Infrastructure Integration (VII) in the US - Enhancing Safety, Enabling Mobility
publicationTitle: The Instititon of Engineering and Technology Seminar on RFID and Electronic Vehicle Identification in Road Transport
abstract: VII or vehicle infrastructure initiative is listed as new DSRC protocol, but it is more than DSRC, it is a major advancement in ITS for vehicle to vehicle and vehicle to roadside systems. The VII 5.9 GHz WAVE protocol provides the range, throughput capacity and low latency to handle current and future ITS roles and capabilities. The VII WAVE protocol integrated into the vehicle's data bus and combined with current and future e-payment systems has the potential to provide tolling, priority toll/HOV lanes, congestion charging and distance-time-location based services

articleTitle: Requirements for a National EVI System
publicationTitle: The Instititon of Engineering and Technology Seminar on RFID and Electronic Vehicle Identification in Road Transport
abstract: The requirements for a National EVI System are presented, which focused on vehicle identification for security and enforcement. In developing EVI technologies some standards are also developed. EVI and DSRC overlap where radio standards are not essential. EVI tag/reader cost is generally lower than DSRC

articleTitle: Collaborations Among In-Vehicle and Infrastructure-Based Sensing Technology for Automotive Applications: The EMMA and TRACKSS EU Projects

abstract: The new synergetic approach to sensing data for automative applications are presented. Software development to build networks of non-homogeneous technologies are discussed. Approach dealing with parts of the engine, detectors within the car and the car itself in connection to the outside world are also presented

abstract: The limited use (low cost) smart tickets are discussed. When would you use them and who's using them are stated in this paper. The business case and cost issues and how they co-exist with smart cards are presented

articleTitle: Customers First - EVI Improving Driver Information
publicationTitle: The Instititon of Engineering and Technology Seminar on RFID and Electronic Vehicle Identification in Road Transport
abstract: The use of automatic number plate recognition to supply real-time traffic condition information is discussed. The development of variable message signs to relay live journey delay times to travelling public is presented. How real-time journey time information was published via Webpage and to mobile devices is also discussed
